title: Motivation: Definition & Theories
summary: Motivation defined and major theories: drive-reduction (Hull), arousal, incentive and cognitive theories, with biological and psychological foundations.
objectives: Describe drive-reduction, arousal, incentive and cognitive theories.
revision: Motivation: definition and major theories — drive-reduction (Hull), arousal, incentive, cognitive — with comparisons and Hull's formula.
traps: Drive-reduction: need → drive → behaviour → goal → homeostasis (Hull).

notes.t: The processes that initiate, direct and sustain behaviour toward satisfying needs or achieving goals.
Physiological needs create drives (tension states); behaviour aims to reduce the drive and restore homeostasis. Hull's formula: Ser = E × D × H × K × J × sl × Dyn − sIr − sLr − sLax.
People seek an optimal level of arousal — too little leads to boredom/sensation-seeking, too much leads to anxiety; performance follows the Yerkes–Dodson curve.
External goals and rewards (incentives) pull behaviour, even in the absence of internal deprivation.
Expectations, goals and beliefs about outcomes motivate behaviour (expectancy-value approaches).
UGC NET frequently asks to compare drive-reduction, arousal, incentive and cognitive theories of motivation.

mnemonics.title: DAIC
mnemonics.text: D — Drive reduction (Hull), A — Arousal (optimal level), I — Incentive (external rewards), C — Cognitive (goals/expectations)

flashcards.a: Processes that initiate, direct and sustain behaviour toward goals.
Needs create drives; behaviour reduces drives (Hull).
